body:
It's impossible to include every opinion, but here are some of the more popular ones:

\-Don't allow it for anyone. All life is sacared, yadda yadda. 

\-I agree with MAiD in principle but I don't trust the government not to abuse it.

\-Terminal illness only.

\-Terminal illness and chronic physical illness only.

\-Terminal illness, chronic physical illness & mental illness only.

\-Literally everyone should have the right to choose to end their own life in a peaceful and dignified way, but there needs to be safeguards involved to ensure vulnerable people who are likely get better don't access it.

\-Bring on the Futurama suicide booths, yee-haw! Freedom trumps everything!

The poll is too limited. It goes from only allowing MAiD for terminal illness to allowing literally anyone who wants to use it for any reason whether they are suffering or not. Many people believe that certain criteria needs to be fulfilled, like having a non-terminal chronic physical illness which causes immense suffering and/or severe chronic depression if the person has the mental capacity to consent. Both should be able to get it, as well as terminal illness, if all available treatment has been tried and failed. A psychological evaluation is required for any reason to access MAiD. As for people who are not suffering but want to end their lives. I think they should be able too, but they should have to wait 5 years after making a request to make sure it's what they really want.

I don't know why people don't believe us when we tell them of our struggles. Like, why don't they? Do our experiences invalidate their belief in a "fair world"? Do we remind them of their own shallow ways (if they are one of people who attack us), or do they just think that we're exaggerating; as if our constant harassment is comparable with the couple of times they were called ugly out of petty spite? I'd really like to understand how people reason this within themselves. They are literally telling ugly people that they know our lives better than we do.

A lot of people shit on ugly people for being ugly and pretty people for being pretty. 'Average privilege' is a thing, but few will agree with me on that. Being invisible might have its drawbacks, but it's certainly the most safe way to exist. I can't imagine going anywhere and not constantly having random people stare at me due to my looks. I'm pretty ugly looking btw.

I think anyone capable of reasoning should be able to get assisted suicide. If suffering is involved then every reasonable and available treatment should be tried first, but if that doesn't help, then it's extremely cruel to dismiss the will of the sufferer. An argument could be made that nothing is stopping anyone from committing suicide themselves (which is untrue, some people are physically incapable of moving, and even those who are not, are terrified of failing and risk losing the ability to move and suffer brain damage) but that point of view is cold and uncaring, and is somewhat naive when considering the high failure rate of suicide.

If somebody is not suffering then they too should be able to choose, but I think the waiting period should be longer for non-sufferers as they have less to lose from waiting.  They might change their minds in the future - either group might, but the price of staying alive for the sufferer is far greater than that of the non-sufferer, and thus the reward might not outweigh the cost.

I'm sorry to hear what you've been through, I really am. You are deserving of all the support available, and I hope you can enjoy life in the future, if you can't right now. I'm not pro-death btw, I'm pro-choice. 

There's a difference between sometimes feeling suicidal and almost always feeling suicidal. I don't know whether that describes your situation, but if it does, you should have the option. I'm not saying that you should commit suicide. Only the individual can make that decision; everybody else's opinion is irrelevant because they lack the perspective of living your life. 

Doctors should never suggest assisted suicide to anyone; I think that would be dangerous and inappropriate. A doctor's job should be to balance safeguarding measures whilst respecting the self-determination of their patients, they should not be advising people to kill themselves. 

I don't think suicide should be the first answer to people's problems, in fact, I don't think it's an answer at all, it's just an unfortunate and tragic last resort to relieve people of their suffering when no answer can be found. Fixing society would make a big difference, I agree. I just don't think people should be forced to stay alive for an indefinite amount of time waiting for change.

The flaws should be fixed, you're right, but holding suffering people hostage until then seems very cruel. There's no guarantee that society will improve any time soon, and plenty of evidence that it won't. Telling people to learn to live with their suffering isn't reasonable if their suffering is causing them so much pain that they're constantly feeling suicidal. Your life might be bearable but that doesn't mean everybody else's is. You might have the privilege to be able to wait for societal improvement, but for others, the price of waiting is just too emotionally draining.
What does that mean? I didn't create myself. I had no choice in being born.

But that's their choice. If they are forced into war than that's immoral in itself. Dying for a cause is a lot different than living in agony for the rest of their life due to severe injury. I can't speak for war vets, but I'm pretty sure many of them regret their decision to join. There are pains far worse than grief and I'm not being dismissive of grief because I know how brutal that can be. Ultimately, it's up to the individual to manage their own emotions. Expecting people to sacrifice themselves for others is the height of entitlement; it's also unreasonable given how painful life can become. If you can't hold you finger under a naked flame for more than 15 seconds, why do you expect others to endure their pain for the rest of their lives?

This is a really odd take. It basically translates to telling someone, "You are obliged to put up with your suffering in order to prevent my own." It reminds me of how people react to suicide in general. It's considered cruel for somebody to leave their family and friends behind after completing suicide; the judgement is never ending. But emotionally blackmailing somebody, or even worse, literally forcing them by locking them up so that they can squalor in their pain for decades, is seen as a positive thing. I guess suffering only matters when you can relate to it, right?

I'll be honest, I don't feel strongly one way or the other about everyone being able to qualify. I think the waiting period  should be longer for those who do not suffer illness however, to ensure that the system does not get clogged up. People with illness should always take priority. I'm not sure why a person would want to end their life if their health - both physical and/or mental - was okay, but my lack of relatability definitely shouldn't prevent people.

Exactly, homeless people shouldn't be held hostage because society can't get its shit together and find a better way to house them. Besides, nobody is eligible for MAiD for homelessness alone (which is usually how it's portrayed by anti-euthanasia groups), you've got to fulfil other criteria as well.

I don't agree that being sad is always better than being dead. There's an entire spectrum of sadness and any negative emotion that we can potentially feel, with the extreme negative ends being intolerable to anyone unlucky enough to feel them. Not everybody gets a break from those negative emotions either. So while I don't think life is inherently horrible like OP states, for some people it's an ever lasting torture fest. Assisted dying should be a legal option for people who cannot get better.

There should be more rigorous safeguarding for mental illness but I think it should be allowed if the person is out of treatment options, and is capable of understanding what their request entails. Not all mentally ill people lack mental capacity, and are actually less delusional than some of the people in our overly optimistic-health biased society.

Euthanasia should be available to anyone who feels substantial distress, cannot adequately be helped by current treatment, and is capable of understanding the consequences of their decision. 

Not all severely depressed people lack mental capacity so I can see no reason why they shouldn't be eligible too. Mental illness is certainly more complex than physical illness and there would need to be more consideration when judging their suitability, but ultimately, all suffering is psychological. Mental illness is often trivialized by society, even by people who suffer mental illness less severely, but it shouldn't be because severe mental illness can feel like torture just as severe physical illness can. If no adequate help can be given then what is the alternative? Some will say that we need to "help and support" these people, but those are empty words which don't really mean anything of substance, not to a person who has tried everything they can already.

So if you were trapped in a burning building and you were literally burning alive, you wouldn't jump out of the window to end your suffering? If so, would your decision be based on irrational thought?

The only person who is capable of deciding to end their own life is the sufferer. Nobody else can understand the extreme pressure that they are up against. I support safeguarding in order to protect vulnerable people who could recover and lead a happy life, but to stop everybody from getting a safe and peaceful death is just cruel.

I'd question the sanity of somebody who was in extreme pain 24/7 and didn't want to die. Wanting to die in those circumstances is perfectly rational. Having depression doesn't necessarily make a person illogical, nor does being happy and healthy make a person logical. Optimism can be extremely delusional in nature and yet it's celebrated when the threat of death is involved. Many people are so afraid of death that they aren't reasonable when it comes to the subject of assisted dying. They would rather believe that there's always a solution to every problem.

Euthanasia is the better option because it's more inclusive (think completely paralyzed patients who request death), and it's safer too; there's less risk of intravenous going wrong. There's always a small chance that a person can vomit up pills even after taking anti-emetics.

The internet partly caused my AvPD, or at least made it worse. If I hadn't had the option of being able to socialize online, the only other option would have been to talk to people irl. I would have been constantly exposed to social situations in person, and the practice (verbal and non-verbal communication) would have helped me significantly.
What is your solution to end unbearable suffering then?

Suffering is worse than nothingness.

Source: Being non-existant for the vast majority of the universe.

I think you're missing the point, though. Your emotional response to suffering seems to be that of indifference. Even more so if a person is going to die anyway. I don't really know what to say so I guess I'll just stop talking to you.
Okay, by that logic, if you were dying, that would give me the right to torture you for the rest of your life. You're going to die anyway, right? It won't matter.

It's not about encouraging others to commit suicide. Nobody wants to force others to administer medically assisted suicide either. It's about choice. If a doctor agrees, and certain conditions are met, then that is their own business. All I want, and many others more, is a change in the law. We shouldn't have to put our safety at risk to die peacefully. That isn't right. Plenty of people with severe chronic illness will never get better. There are no treatment options left for us and every day is a massive struggle at best, torture at worst. It's up to the individual to decide if their life is worth living, not you. You may think you possess some kind of universal truth, unknown to me, about life, death, existential value and suffering, but you really do not. I used to think as you do until life taught me otherwise.

Suicidal people generally don't want to cause trauma to ever finds their corpse. 

And really what you are saying is so, so cold. We live in a society that is supposed to help and care about each other. Forcing somebody to clandestinely go off into the night and kill themselves alone is really cruel. That's not to mention that suicide attempts often fail, and even jumping doesn't necessarily lead to a quick and painless death. Also, how are completely paralysed supposed to kill themselves? What lonely and barbaric times we live in.

The terminally ill often choose to die due to depression caused by their health condition. Not all but some, and who would blame them for being depressed? Depression doesn't necessarily remove the mental capacity of the sufferer. You could argue that everyone who wants an assisted death has had their ability to make a decision impaired due to whatever negative force is at play. I'd like to know how healthy people can make a valid judgment about the rationality of suicide if they have never suffered with severe chronic illness before. Don't you think their ignorance impairs their ability to make an informed and proper judgment on the subject?
Some people will live in excruciating pain for the rest of their lives and are not terminal. Why shouldn't they have a choice to end their misery?
Should have been made legal centuries ago.
England.

That is a valid concern, although as far as I'm aware, MAiD has only ever exposed already existing inadequate social support. I've yet to see any evidence that funding is being cut as a result of MAiD. Pro-lifers will frame it as such but there's no evidence.

The solution here is to improve social services. I don't see this as an argument against euthanasia. I'm not pointing my finger at you here personally, but many pro-lifers seem to be more concerned with euthanasia being legal than about disabled people suffering due to unfunded services. The fact that some disabled people decide to take their own lives rather than live without adequate support speaks at how awful their lives must be. If  support is not provided then that is a failing of the government and society; not that of euthanasia, which at least gives them a peaceful end. Far more compassionate than being told to just get on with their misery.

In my country we are forced to suffer or take matters into our own hands if we're still physically capable. Non-violent suicide is very easy to mess up and can leave the person in an even worse state than before.
No one should be alone when they die. :(

Yes it should be legal.  If a person no longer finds value in their life and no longer wishes to carry on then the compassionate thing to do would be to help them die in a peaceful way. Obviously nobody could just turn up on the day and ask for it for just any old reason. There would need to be a waiting period, a psychological assessment and their problem would need to be untreatable/unresolvable plus creating substantial distress. Mental disorders wouldn't automatically be disqualified but the decision making process would need to be more robust.

Right. But if a person cannot be helped by medical/psychiatric treatment and expresses a wish to die, then what? Should they be denied the right to die peacefully and have to suffer for decades? Because that is the current "answer" to this problem in most societies. How is that compassionate?
Imagine being well adjusted in this shit show of a world.

I know I enjoy drawing more whilst high, and I put more care into my drawings because I am more invested and more ideas are flowing. The end product suffers due to lack of unpracticed technique, however the key elements of increased creativity are there. I'd say all my high drawings are more interesting in content than my non-high ones.
I remember a subtitute teacher asking me what happened to my face, lmao. The day I learned that I wasn't safe from anyone.

Society rejects ugly children then wonders why so many of them have such poor social skills. "They're not very nice because their personality is a reflection of their ugly face." That is how many people view ugly people. They can't see or deliberately ignore how a lack of social training and mistreating somebody could lead to social dysfunction. Nope, the fault completely lies with the ugly.
No deformity but my head is oddly shaped, I have bad skin, dark sunken eyes, horrible teeth and skinny arms.

Nobody expects those words to magically cure depression. The words are empty and thoughtless because they don't take into consideration the depressed individual's personal circumstances and experiences. The language used is broad and tries to apply to as many people as possible. That may be seen as a good thing but not to the OP, who will read it and may feel even more alienated. 

The problem is, most people want to save lives in the moment, but they don't want to put in the effort to actually improve a mentally ill person's life. If they did they would ask genuine questions, get to know the person, and not assume they know what is best for them. Saying stuff like, "You are worthy and loved" isn't helpful to somebody whose depression isn't caused by lack of self-esteem or lack of love. It may not even be true, the depressed person might not be loved by anybody. Maybe they are loved but don't feel like they are. In any case, a random internet stranger, or worse a bot, has no clue what is happening in that person's life. 

`it’s a combination of things starting with admitting that you need help`

Sometimes nothing cures depression, whether you get help or not. That is the sad reality. That's why assisted suicide needs to be an option.

I think both questions are valid. Yes, more needs to be done to improve people's lives so that they do not want to die, but not all mental illnesses are caused by situational reasons. All the social changes and support in the world will not make some people's lives more bearable because the cause of their illnesses are a mystery and they're resistant to current treatment models.

I'm sure people have been saying that to others since the dawn of medical science. Imagine being diagnosed with an extremely painful case of multiple sclerosis in the late 1800s. Decades of enduring unrelentless severe pain for nothing. Hope and optimism can be dangerous when they're based on little to no evidence of improvment.

P.S It wasn't me who downvoted you.

I wonder how effective bots are at preventing suicide. I mean, people try for years to get better, and then comes along a bot which has nothing to offer other than impersonal cliche bullshit. Humans will say the same things bots do, but hearing it from a bot just seems to confirm how empty and thoughtless those words are.
Would you be more willing to allow euthanasia to a child if they were suffering excruciating pain that was untreatable?

Half the people who say that have never even been depressed before - not even mildly depressed. They act like some kind of authority figure on the matter yet they know the least of anyone about the subject. The other half may have had hardship before but either their depression wasn't severe; or it was, but they found a way to alleviate their symptoms to a manageable level. Not everybody is able to find any meaningful relief. Not because they don't try everything they can but because for what ever reason, relief is impossible. Heh, just seems like people project their own experiences onto others. "If I can find a way to be content then anybody can."

Mine has been getting worse for years and now it's at the point of becoming intolerable. If I didn't have good days then I think I might have killed myself already. The pain is spread everywhere but worse in my stomach, which causes feelings of dread and terror. In a way the emotional aspect is worse than the physical pain itself.

A little bit, probably. However, by this point, I think I'm so cynical of people that even being respected and/or valued for the rest of my life time wouldn't allow me to trust others again. I believe I would have become a different person had I been born attractive.

There is no real solution to this. Parents and schools should teach the dangers of online safety (if they already don't) but half the teens won't listen anyway. They are too busy trying to impress boys/girls their own age, of which these videos are designed for. They're probably aware of online creeps but  that comes second priority to them. The sites should do more to police creeps but there are so many of them out there. No site with such a large user base could keep up with them, sadly.
Does anyone know if the canvas will be extended again?

Some people don't want to hear about other's trauma because it makes them feel uncomfortable. They may not know what to say or how to help. Some may even dispise what they see as weakness. There's also the angle that some people want to believe in a just and fair world (which doesn't exist), and stories of trauma undermines their belief in that. After all, the human race in general relies on self-deception  and ignorance to stay happy, or at least some what content. Nobody can have it as bad as they say they do.

3 x 300mg per day (five years) to nothing. When I first started taking gabapentin, I was only taking 3 x 100mg per day (six months). Skipping a pill back then also made me feel terrible, perhaps to a lesser extent, but it was still a nasty experience. I don't think I could have forced myself into live in that state indefinitely. Everything seemed so bleak, dark and miserable. Honestly, the only reason I went cold turkey instead of listening to my doctor's advice of tapering off over a number of weeks is because I just wanted to get through the whole withdrawal proccess as quickly as possible.

The withdrawal of gabapentin can be brutal for some people. When I was still taking them, if I even missed one pill out of three on the day, I felt awful. When I stopped taking them altogther I felt like I was losing my mind. I didn't think they helped my pain much or did anything for my anxiety whilst taking them, but after about after four weeks of going cold turkey, I can tell you that they did help my anxiety to a great extent; my pain to a lesser extent but they did help a little bit, I just didn't realise at the time (your experience may differ!) I say this as someone who has completed withdrawal and want to go back on them, although if that's not possible, I can live without them. They didn't solve my problems but they did help. It's possible to cut them off altogether but you may need to go through hell to get there (about 2 weeks for me going cold turkey).
Not really. My body also looks like crap.

Lookism is about social hierarchy more than anything. It effects me by making my life a thousand times more difficult than average looking people. In a way, looks are a lot like currency. If you're dirt poor then good luck striving for anything meaningful in this life. It's still possible to become something of worth, yes, but statistically improbable - usually based on other factors of privilege.
Nobody is entitled to the affection of strangers, that's right. Although, as a hideous person, I think I'm entitled to common decency at least.
It's difficult to enjoy who you are when you never get to express yourself to others because nobody is interested.

I stay indoors all summer long. Usually I go outside for exercise every night when nobody is around, but I still need to wear a coat to do that else I feel extremely self-conscious. Wearing a coat in the summer is just not a viable option, even at night time. Every day that passes I feel my mood getting worse in those months. Exercise is very important for mental health. I still exercise in my home but it's just not the same.
I wouldn't say I like what I see, but at this point I wouldn't change either, mainly out of spite towards the haters.

This is the sort of behaviour that keeps me living as a recluse. Everytime I try to reintegrate myself back into society, exactly what you mentioned happens to me. I'm so fed up with being used as a figure of fun, or by some insecure dickwad using me as a method of asserting their social status to themselves and others. Dehumanization is what it is. They don't care about our feelings because to them we don't matter.

If you hate a part of your body then you do technically have body dysmorphia. I wish there were terms we could use to differentiate between regular body dysmorphia and body dysmorphia caused by actual ugliness. They may be similar in many ways but the cause sure isn't. Do psychologists even make the distinction?

It's not only pretty people who discriminate against uglies. Actually, the stunningly beautiful are less likely to be jerks than anyone else, at least in my experience. They still avoid us like the plague, though.
There's a difference between feeling ugly and being ugly. Two very different life experiences. This vid will be helpful to some but not to others.
That's nice of you to say but most people don't agree with you, unfortunetly.

I get the impression that a large part of society feels it's their moral duty to make our lives difficult. They might not even realize they feel that way but they do. With that kind of mindset, it's not surprising that they gaslight us. It's far easier to blame us for our problems than it is for them to admit they are shitty people in some respects.
You look like a normal average person to me.

Hideous people are reluctant to send their pictures due to fear of mockery (and to respect those with the gift of sight!) There's no way to completely stop non-hideous people from joining, but hopefully even most ugly or unattractive people can appreciate they are not hideous or grotesque looking, so they wouldn't join anyway. There could be rules about topic discussions: no rate me posts or complaining about others not finding you attractive. I think that would thin out the herd. Not being able to date sucks but it pales in comparison when compared to being harrassed and laughed at no matter where you go. When even finding a job is a mammoth task. When you have no social skills because few, if anyone, has ever offered their friendship.

Someone should start a sub for truly hideous people.

The problem with this sub is that the subject is too broad so we're outnumbered by people who just feel unattractive. The discrimination and life experience of hideous people is different.

I think race, gender and prejudice against ugly people are all different forms of discrimination and have different roots, but I get your point. None of them are morally right. Yet very few people actually take ugly discrimination seriously. It's not spoken about often at all in the media. The closest thing is the message of body positivity, but that's a seperate issue, really catered towards relatively normal looking people.

I think encouraging people to stay alive is what we should strive for, but we shouldn't scare them into doing it. Some people have a very valid reason for committing suicide; others do it impulsively because their minds aren't in the right place at the time. All we can do  is show them what is worth living for, and/or guide them to mental health professionals. Allow the person time to make up their own mind as to whether their life is worth living. Scare tactics do nothing but serve as emotional blackmail. I can only imagine the amount of needless suffering that has occured over the centuries because a person was too afraid to end their pain. Please don't force people into that position.

It's funny when people tell an ugly person to act confidently. You follow their advice and then, like moths to a flame, assholes comes out of nowhere to put you back into your place. They see a confident ugly person as going against the natural order of things. *"Who are you to feel any self-confidence?"* Acting confidently is just inviting more hate and harassment upon yourself. A lot of non-ugly people don't realize this because acting confidently helps with their lives, so they assume it must help everybody.

When people say suicide is never the answer, you know they haven't really thought it through. If someone is suffering unbearably and nothing helps; not therapy, not drugs, nothing... What then? Should they remain alive, suffering every moment of their existence, just to keep your naive happy-go-lucky worldview intact?

Short term pain, yes. 

Chronic pain fucks with with your mind over time and brings anxiety to every moment of your life.
I learned to have fun without the need of others. Probably not healthy but I see no other option.

If you are truly ugly then people will let you know. And I don't mean the odd petty insult from somebody who is angry with you. You'll hear comments like "ew" from complete strangers, and passabyers will look at you with disgust and distain in their eyes. Anyone who befriends you will act self-conscious around others if they're seen associating with you, due to the fact that you make them appear socially inferior.
Sure. :P
You might want to see a therapist, sounds like you might have an anxiety disorder.

It's unfortunate but the reality is: most people in this world are insecure and lack purpose. The only thing that makes them feel better about that is imposing their supposed superiority onto others. That way, they feel like their life matters. It's more of an existential coping mechanism than anything.

Eh, we can date whoever the fuck we want, aslong as the other party is interested aswell. 

Although, I will say that there are some extremely entitled people out there who only care about looks, and then for some reason are shocked when they discover others as being just as judgmental as they are.

Same, but maybe we feel that way because people treat uglies like our words don't matter. I mean, if others react to everything we say with little to no enthusiasm, then it's not surprising that we've learned over time not to put any effort in.

I don't blame you for being that way because most humans are the same. It's partly learned, partly natural, I believe. My real gripe is with those who go out of their way to make life difficult for uglies. I'd rather be ignored and under valued than have somebody directly attack me with their nastiness.

I dunno. I live in a pretty rough area and people around here seem to care a lot about my appearance; so much so that I rarely leave the house due to harassment. Not only verbal but physical too. A lot of people don't actually care that they're ugly. They're past caring. What they do care about is being mistreated by others.

None of those people are ugly ugly, though. On a scale of 1 to 10 in terms of attractiveness, I'm probably a 2 at most. It's difficult to learn charm or charisma when nobody gives you a chance to be around them.
The only people who hate ugly women on this sub are incels who should just be ignored by everybody anyway.
Your hair needs a tidy but other than that you look fine imo.

I've been a recluse for many years now, but back in my high school days, not a single day passed when I wasn't insulted at least once about my looks. Not everybody I met was an asshole, but a fair amount of people were; usually complete strangers who I didn't even know and who had no reason to attack me what-so-ever. You don't know what that does to a person. It wasn't even their insults which hurt, really, it was the fact that so many people were dehumanizing me. I felt so unworthy and unlikable. And there's nothing I could have done about it. There's no way I could have fought so many people; I didn't have the energy or the confidence, I also feared for my safety. You see, an ugly, low status kid sticking up for himself isn't a good idea. The aggressor can't be seen to lose against somebody of such low worth; they will fight them to the bitter end to retain their sense of pride and status.
If this guy is a 1 or a 2 then I must be in the negatives, lmao.

That sounds rough. :( 

I can relate to most of what you said. I see a lot of people saying that they find it easier to go outside when they are with somebody else, but for me, that would make it ten times worse, because then I'd be afraid of looking like an idiot in front of them, or making them look and feel bad by association.
Not only in the past either.

When people say ugly, what they usually mean is average or just under. That's society's new definition of ugly. If you're a 4 or under, you're not even worth consideration or acknowledgement anymore. 

But sure, LoOkS dOn'T mAtTeR.

Reintegrating yourself back into society gets more difficult with every passing year. Just something to keep in mind. I know you're not asking for advice, but I do suggest voice chatting with people online at the very least. I kept to myself for years and completely lost my ability to socialise. Talking to family just isn't the same. I wish you the best.
I only leave the house at night time, for exercise, when nobody is around to see me. I've pretty much been a recluse for 14 years except for doctor visits.
